metas.name: Annihilation
metas.description:
Captures a zone that refracts everything that passes through it. A team enters the Shimmer, where light, radio, DNA and memory are mixed across channels like a signal through a prism — plants shaped like people, animals carrying other species' traits.

A biologist signs up for a dangerous, secret expedition in which the laws of nature don't apply.

metas.name: Possession
metas.description:
Captures a marriage breaking down as literal hysteria. A couple in Berlin tearing each other apart, in Isabelle Adjani's unhinged performance — domestic, then completely not.

A woman starts exhibiting increasingly disturbing behavior after asking her husband for a divorce. Suspicions of infidelity soon give way to something much more sinister.

metas.name: Perfect Blue
metas.description:
Captures fame eating a person's grip on which self is hers. A pop idol turned actress, a stalker, and a fan site narrating her life in first person — the animated form is what makes the slippage work.

A pop singer gives up her career to become an actress, but she slowly goes insane when she starts being stalked by an obsessed fan and what seems to be a ghost of her past.

metas.name: Cure
metas.description:
Captures emptiness spreading from person to person. A Tokyo detective investigates murders where each killer is different, calm, and cannot explain themselves — hypnotic and grey rather than jumpy.

A frustrated detective deals with the case of several gruesome murders committed by people who have no recollection of what they've done.

metas.name: The Witch
metas.description:
Captures religious paranoia eating a family from inside its own beliefs. Puritan settlers exiled to a forest's edge: a crop fails, a baby vanishes, and their theology gives them only one interpretation.

An isolated Puritan family in 1630s New England comes unraveled by the forces of witchcraft and possession.

metas.name: Lake Mungo
metas.description:
Captures grief in the form of a family documentary. Found footage, but the subject is not the ghost — it is parents and a brother in interviews, months after a drowning, still looking for anything.

Strange things start happening after a girl is found drowned in a lake.

metas.name: Safe
metas.description:
Captures a suburban life so empty a woman becomes allergic to modernity itself. In perfect pastel houses, symptoms no doctor can find, and a drift toward a desert self-help commune.

An affluent and unexceptional homemaker in the suburbs develops multiple chemical sensitivity.

metas.name: Hereditary
metas.description:
Captures a family where grief and resentment were already there before anything supernatural. A grandmother dies, a mother builds miniature scenes of her life, and a dinner-table argument is the scariest sequence.

A grieving family is haunted by tragic and disturbing occurrences.

metas.name: Leviathan
metas.description:
Captures commercial fishing as a sensory ordeal. Cameras strapped to nets, chains, helmets and the hull of a North Atlantic trawler — fish heads, gulls, diesel, men half-asleep at 3 a.m., no explanation offered.

A documentary shot in the North Atlantic and focused on the commercial fishing industry.

metas.name: Under the Skin
metas.description:
Captures human beings seen from outside the species. A woman drives a van around Glasgow picking up men, in real streets with hidden cameras and non-actors, and something in the routine begins to fail — images that lodge permanently.

A mysterious young woman seduces lonely men in the evening hours in Scotland. However, events lead her to begin a process of self-discovery.

metas.name: Funny Games
metas.description:
Captures the audience's appetite, by refusing to feed it the usual way. Two polite young men hold a family at their holiday house; violence happens off-screen or gets rewound, and the film keeps asking why you're still watching.

Two violent young men take a mother, father, and son hostage in their vacation cabin and force them to play sadistic "games" with one another for their own amusement.

metas.name: Videodrome
metas.description:
Captures a TV signal getting inside a body. A sleazy Toronto cable programmer finds a pirate broadcast of torture, becomes obsessed, and his perception and flesh start reorganising around it.

A Toronto cable TV station co-owner who specializes in adult entertainment searches for the producers of a dangerous and bizarre broadcast titled "Videodrome."

metas.name: A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night
metas.description:
Captures a vampire film rebuilt from Iranian, Western and skate-punk parts. A fictional Iranian ghost town, a chador-wearing vampire on a skateboard, a drug dealer and a cat, in long black-and-white silences between bursts of pop.

In the Iranian ghost-town Bad City, a place that reeks of death and loneliness, the townspeople are unaware they are being stalked by a lonesome vampire.

metas.name: Pi
metas.description:
Captures obsession with a pattern, filmed on grain. A mathematician in a tiny New York apartment with computers made of junk, a number that Wall Street and a Hasidic sect both want, and migraines rendered as drill sounds.

A paranoid mathematician searches for a key number that will unlock the universal patterns found in nature.

metas.name: Audition
metas.description:
Captures loneliness curdling into horror by changing genre mid-film. A widower holds fake auditions to find a wife; the first hour is a sad, gentle drama before the film reveals what it actually was.

A widower has his film producer friend organize a fake audition as a means of helping him find a new girlfriend, but the woman he selects is not who she appears to be.

metas.name: The Lighthouse
metas.description:
Captures two men rotting in each other's company. A rock in a storm, gaslight, seagull taboos, and two keepers descending into myth, flatulence and murder inside a frame almost square enough to be a trap.

Two lighthouse keepers try to maintain their sanity while living on a remote and mysterious New England island in the 1890s.

metas.name: The Act of Seeing with One's Own Eyes
metas.description:
Captures the camera reduced to pure looking: Brakhage films autopsies in a Pittsburgh morgue silently and in close-up, with no commentary to hide behind, asking whether there is anything a camera should refuse to see.

At a morgue, forensic pathologists conduct autopsies of the corpses assigned. "S. Brakhage, entering, WITH HIS CAMERA, one of the forbidden, terrific locations of our culture, the autopsy room. It is a place wherein, inversely, life is cherished, for it exists to affirm that no one of us may die without our knowing exactly why. All of us, in the person of the coroner, must see that, for ourselves, with our own eyes. It is a room full of appalling particular intimacies, the last ditch of individuation. Here our vague nightmare of mortality acquires the names and faces of OTHERS. This last is a process that requires a WITNESS; and what 'idea' may finally have inserted itself into the sensible world we can still scarcely guess, for the CAMERA would seem the perfect Eidetic Witness, staring with perfect compassion where we can scarcely bear to glance." – Hollis Frampton

metas.name: Häxan
metas.description:
Captures a lecture dissolving into delirium. Christensen's silent Swedish study of witchcraft keeps abandoning its own lecture format for re-enactments — sabbaths, torture chambers, possessed nuns — and from 1922 remains wilder than most folk horror made since.

Fictionalized documentary showing the evolution of witchcraft, from its pagan roots to its confusion with hysteria in Eastern Europe.

metas.name: The Wicker Man
metas.description:
Captures paganism not as horror but as joy. A devout Christian policeman arrives on a Scottish island where the harvest failed and the old religion quietly resumed — and the islanders keep bursting into song, which is what makes the ending land.

A puritan police sergeant arrives in a Scottish island village in search of a missing girl, who the pagan locals claim never existed.

metas.name: Kwaidan
metas.description:
Captures folklore as pure painted atmosphere. Kobayashi adapts Lafcadio Hearn's ghost tales on vast studio sets — a snow spirit, a blind biwa player performing for the dead — the closest Japanese equivalent to Parajanov's tableau method.

A collection of four Japanese folk tales with supernatural themes.

metas.name: The Company of Wolves
metas.description:
Captures the folk tale's actual content — appetite, danger, metamorphosis — that the children's versions politely remove. Jordan and Angela Carter nest werewolf tales inside a sleeping girl's dream, all fog, forests and practical-effect transformations.

A teenage girl in a country manor falls asleep while reading a magazine, and has a disturbing dream involving wolves prowling the woods below her bedroom window.
